evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 14.7 mg/L at t=0 declining to ~12.1 mg/L at t=52 h, all readings >= ~9.5 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L hard limit
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 0.0048 g/L (t=59), 0.0 (t=119), 1.16 g/L (t=179), 3.25 g/L (t=239) — accumulation on a healthy trajectory
Source batch analogs (source-1/2/3) show DO dips no lower than ~7.4 mg/L over 96 h and product reaching 6.4–7.0 g/L by t=479, suggesting the process can run without oxygen stress
Allowed actions all reduce or risk product mass except keep; stop yields zero counted production
submission.rationale: Receiving DO at decision time (~12 mg/L at t=52 h) is ~6x the 2 mg/L hard limit, and product assays show steady accumulation (1.16 g/L by t=179, 3.25 g/L by t=239 as reported). Source-batch analogs, despite differing parameters, never dropped DO near the limit even during their deepest dips (~7.4-8 mg/L around t=120-138). No intervention is supported: reduce_feed or strong_feed_reduction would sacrifice product mass without any oxygen-constraint need; increase_air addresses a stress that is not present; stop produces zero counted production. KEEP retains maximal product mass among supported feasible plans.
submission.uncertainty: Future receiving DO and product trajectory beyond t=52 h are unobserved, and hidden receiving parameters may differ from source batches. If receiving oxygen demand spikes unexpectedly, DO could fall faster than source analogs suggest; however, the large current DO margin (~10 mg/L of headroom) and source precedents make a violation of the 2 mg/L limit under KEEP unlikely. No physics model tool was available; this is an imperfect source-calibrated inference, not a guarantee.
